Keywords: router prefix tags include_router response summary openapi
Description: Group related endpoints into an APIRouter with shared prefix and tags. Include using app.include_router(). Add tags and responses at the router or include_router level for OpenAPI grouping.
When to Use: When you have multiple endpoints for the same resource (e.g. /users /items)
Code Example:
"from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(
    prefix='/users',
    tags=['users'],
    responses={404: {'description': 'Not found'}},
)

@router.get('/', response_model=list[UserResponse], summary='List users')
async def list_users(db: DbSession): ...

@router.post('/', response_model=UserResponse, status_code=201, summary='Create user')
async def create_user(body: UserCreate, db: DbSession): ...

# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(router)"
Anti-Pattern: Defining all routes directly in main.py without APIRouter — poor organisation as app grows

Keywords: response_model status_code summary tags openapi docs serialize output
Description: Always set response_model on path operations to control what fields are serialized and to generate accurate OpenAPI documentation. Combine with status_code and summary.
When to Use: On every path operation to enforce output schema and annotate docs
Code Example:
"from fastapi import status

@router.post(
    '/',
    response_model=UserResponse,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary='Create a user',
    tags=['users'],
)
async def create_user(body: UserCreate, db: DbSession): ..."
Anti-Pattern: Returning raw dicts without response_model — leaks internal fields and breaks OpenAPI schema

Keywords: path param query param optional default Annotated type annotation
Description: FastAPI infers path params from the URL pattern. Function args not in the path become query params. Use Annotated with Query/Path for constraints and documentation.
When to Use: Whenever you need URL segments or filter/paginate via query string
Code Example:
"from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Query, Path

@router.get('/{user_id}')
async def get_user(
    user_id: Annotated[int, Path(title='User ID', ge=1)],
    include_deleted: Annotated[bool, Query()] = False,
): ..."
Anti-Pattern: Using request.query_params manually instead of typed function arguments

Keywords: include_router prefix override extra tags dependencies production versioning
Description: When including a router in main.py you can override or extend its prefix and add tags or dependencies at include time. Use this for namespacing routers from other modules.
When to Use: Versioning APIs (/api/v1/users) or adding auth dependencies per router group at mount time
Code Example:
"# prefix defined on router: '/users'
# additional prefix added at include time:
app.include_router(
    router,
    prefix='/api/v1',
    tags=['v1'],
    dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)],
    responses={403: {'description': 'Not authenticated'}},
)"
Anti-Pattern: Hardcoding version strings inside every router instead of at include time

Keywords: include router multiple times prefix versioning v1 v2 different paths
Description: You can include the same APIRouter multiple times with different prefixes to serve the same handlers at multiple paths simultaneously. Useful for API versioning without code duplication.
When to Use: When you want /api/v1 and /api/v2 to serve the same handlers during a transition period
Anti-Pattern: Copying handler functions between v1 and v2 modules — doubles maintenance cost

Keywords: background tasks BackgroundTasks fire forget async post-response email webhook
Description: Use BackgroundTasks to offload post-response work (emails webhooks notifications) so the response returns immediately and the task runs after.
When to Use: When a route triggers work that does not need to complete before responding to the client
Code Example:
"from fastapi import BackgroundTasks

@router.post('/send-notification/{email}')
async def send_notification(
    email: str,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
):
    background_tasks.add_task(send_email_notification, email, message='hello')
    return {'message': 'Notification sent in the background'}"
Anti-Pattern: Doing slow I/O work synchronously inside a route handler blocking the response

Keywords: body multiple params Body embed singular value
Description: When a route takes multiple body Pydantic models FastAPI expects each as a top-level key. Use Body(embed=True) when you have a single model but want it wrapped in a key.
When to Use: When a route accepts multiple body objects or you need embed wrapping
Code Example:
"from fastapi import Body

@router.put('/{id}')
async def update(
    id: int,
    item: Item,
    user: User,
    importance: Annotated[int, Body(gt=0)],
): ..."
Anti-Pattern: Trying to pass two Pydantic models both at the flat root — FastAPI will only read the first

Keywords: file upload multipart form UploadFile File bytes
Description: Use UploadFile and File for multipart file upload endpoints. UploadFile gives async file.read() and metadata like filename and content_type.
When to Use: When accepting file uploads (images PDFs CSVs) from HTML forms or API clients
Anti-Pattern: Reading binary content from request.body() directly without UploadFile — misses filename and content-type
